tools.name: V2 Receipt Verifier

tools.name: NameMath Art Contracts

evidence.value: 20 rows: forward then inverse is the identity over 845 grid points across five seeds, and the map is injective on the grid
every generated affine over 400 seeds has determinant +1 or -1, so the inverse is an integer map
64 seeds produce 64 distinct transform programs, and a one-character name change leaves 0 of 49 cells unchanged

limitations: namemath.vy had never compiled before this commit: convert(block.prevrandao, bytes32) is a type error in every Vyper 0.4.x
no declared coordinate bound: the safe grid is a property of the seed, measured at 158 on the worst of 24 namemath seeds against 1727786871 on logobackground
namemath's register() mixes caller-supplied entropy with a readable prevrandao, so a minter can grind the seed; 256 candidates reachable in one transaction gave 13 distinct trait classes
logobackground's `if m < 0` guard after a sum of squares is unreachable under checked arithmetic; the case it appears to handle reverts instead
namemath binds no name: its registry seed contains no name, contract, chain id or algorithm version
art, not settlement. Neither contract touches ENS, Uniswap, a pool, a token or a payment
not deployed anywhere, and not audited

tools.name: ENSv2 Configuration Builder

evidence.value: 136 rows in the ENS suite, of which about 60 cover the builder: one positive path, ten classified refusals, and every committed field moved one at a time

five sabotages killed by their own named row: an accepted recipient override, a bypassed payout allowlist, a removed staleness check, a diagnostic that crept into the commitment, and a failed resolution built anyway

limitations: it builds a commitment; it does not resolve, sign, quote or settle
the payout allowlist is one token on one chain, compiled in rather than configurable
staleness is judged against a block the CALLER supplies, so a caller that lies about the head gets a stale configuration
the block window bounds a quote deadline through Ethereum's twelve-second slot, which is conservative but is a protocol assumption stated rather than proven here
local tests only: no fork run, and V2 is not deployed
not audited

tools.name: Arc Nanopayments Integration

evidence.value: 141 rows, offline: a vector signed by Circle's own SDK at version 2.0.4 verifies against an independent implementation that never imports it
the Gateway authorization signs exactly six fields; resource, request, response, session and cumulative budget are provably outside it
five sabotages killed by their own named row, including one that grades a purchased resource as cryptographically verified
upstream pinned at circlefin/arc-nanopayments a29f920e, Apache-2.0, inspected 2026-09-08

limitations: Circle Gateway batching produces OPERATIONAL ACCOUNTING rather than a per-payment commitment: the SDK contains no merkle root, no batch id, no inclusion proof and no indexable event
settlement evidence is an API assertion of shape success plus transaction, where that transaction is shared by every payment in the batch
a Gateway authorization proves an amount was authorised to a recipient and says nothing about what was bought
the upstream demo uses plain private keys rather than Circle Agent Wallet, and discards the payer signature when it records a payment
no Arc transaction has been sent, no wallet created, no faucet used, and nothing settled
not audited

tools.name: Merchant Settlement Policy (Vyper)

evidence.value: 13 rows: a split loses nothing at fourteen amounts including 0, 1 and 2^64-1, and the last leg is proven to absorb the flooring remainder

eight refusals: shares off ten thousand in four shapes, a zero token, a bank share with no payout reference, a stranger registering, a double registration, a stranger changing a policy, and an unregistered merchant

limitations: PRIOR ART: written before this repository's hackathon window and carried in, not authored during it; see docs/PRIOR-ART.md
policy only: it decides proportions and holds no tokens, moves nothing and pays nobody
the platform address is set at construction and cannot be changed or renounced
the operator address is not checked against zero, so a merchant registered with none can only be changed by the platform
no way to deactivate a merchant once registered
not deployed anywhere, and not audited

tools.name: PayAny Router (Vyper)

evidence.value: 14 rows: the Chainlink gate refuses a missing feed, a zero or negative price, a stale answer, a future-dated answer and an incomplete round, with the freshness boundary checked from both sides
an intent is consumed by id alone, so a replay under a different merchant or amount is still refused

limitations: PRIOR ART: written before this repository's hackathon window and carried in, not authored during it; see docs/PRIOR-ART.md
pay() executes CALLER-SUPPLIED calldata against the Universal Router with a live approval; what bounds the damage is the oracle gate on the measured USDC delta, not any validation of the calldata
the bank leg is approved to the off-ramp and the off-ramp is trusted to pull it: an adapter that does not pull leaves that USDC in the router with a live allowance and pay() still succeeds
no L2 sequencer-uptime check accompanies the Chainlink read
the oracle gate is applied to the gross swap output, while the merchant is paid after the platform fee
the swap leg itself is untested here: it needs a Universal Router, and only the USDC path runs without one
not deployed anywhere, and not audited

tools.name: CRE Liquidation-Protection Policy

evidence.value: 88 offline rows and nine mutations, every one killed by its own named row
all five published scenarios survive every tick with the whole loan kept open, spending between 89 and 231 vETH units of the 500 available and zero vUSD
the untouched starting position is liquidatable at any price at or below 1812.82, which is 9.4 percent below the start

limitations: a policy engine only: it decides, and does not observe a chain, sign, send, or run inside a TEE
the simulation assumes one observation per price update and that every action lands before the organiser's liquidation sweep, neither of which is guaranteed
gas, transaction failure and DON latency are not modelled
no CRE CLI is installed, no workflow is deployed, and join() has not been called
scoring weights are deliberately NOT compiled in: how continuity and capital efficiency trade off is unanswered by the organisers, so the selector stays configurable
not audited

tools.name: CRE Workflow Adapter

evidence.value: 86 offline rows and ten mutations, every one killed
the adapter's decision equals the frozen policy's in 950 compared states across the whole published price range
observing every price update survives the sudden crash; observing every SECOND update loses it

limitations: PUBLIC DEPLOYMENT IS BLOCKED: the challenge README and its own config.staging.json name different lending and token addresses at the pinned commit, and the organisers have not said which is authoritative
there is no default deployment profile and there must not be one; selecting is an argument
local only: nothing is deployed, nothing is broadcast, join() has not been called and no CRE CLI is installed
evidence records are LOCAL_SIMULATION and cannot claim a TEE attestation or a DON execution receipt
whether a cron faster than five minutes is permitted by the DON is not established here
not audited
